entities.title: Cyberspace explorer
entities.summary: A web page that shows a repository's .dev folders (its diagrams drawn, its behavior views and knowledge files written out), and the Worker that serves it at cyberspace-explorer.com.
entities.purpose: Lets a person read what agents keep in a repository's .dev folders (how it is built, what it does and what it knows about itself) in a browser, with nothing to install, clone or run.
boundaries: It reads .dev files (or the one .cyberspace-explorer tree that can stand in for them); it never writes to a repository.
The page is one HTML file with no build step, and does its reading and drawing in the reader's browser. It also works served as a plain file, without sign-in.
The Worker in worker/ serves the page and, when set up, signs readers in with GitHub and reads GitHub for them; it holds no state of its own.
What it reads is defined by the skills in Meta/Agents/Skills and the catalogue in Meta/Agents/Knowledge; when they change, the page follows them.
The copy people use is deployed to cyberspace-explorer.com from main; this repository is its source.
entities.details: The root holds `index.html`, the whole page; `wrangler.jsonc`, which deploys the Worker in `worker/` with the page inside it; `package.json`, whose only script runs the tests in `test/`; and `README.md`, which says how to use it and how it works. Its `.dev/` folder describes the browser itself, as fully as a designer needs to make a pass at it: start with the [design pass](.dev/backlog.json) item, which says what to read in what order.
